titles: Leaves from a 13th-century Oxford Bible with early provenance in a Dominican house in Italy
places: Oxford, England, Great Britain, United Kingdom, Europe (England, Oxford)
manuscript_binding: not sequential, two columns of 43-44 lines numbered ‘3’ or ‘4’ at the bottom of the text block, ruled space: 110 x 65mm, ten illuminated initials in red, pink and blue with white penwork outlined in green to open: (i) II Corinthians (ii) prologue to Galatians; (iii) Galatians; (iv) prologue to Ephesians; (v) Ephesians; (vi) prologue to I Timothy; (vii) I Timothy; (viii) II Timothy; (ix) Philemon; and (x) Hebrews, (arranged as bifolia out of order on archival hinges, a couple of marginal tears).
other_info: Written and illuminated in Oxford around the middle of the 13th century: the leaves have numbering between the columns at every fifth line of text, an exclusively English feature deriving from Oxford, as described by M.A. and R.H. Rouse: ‘The purpose of the line-numbering was to enable the owner of a book to create his own index if he wished, or simply to be able to note down references to parts of books with precision. […] This reference system, still widely used today for classical texts and poetry, in the Middle Ages did not cross the Channel [...]’ (Authentic Witnesses, 1991, pp. 234-36). The removal of the Bible to Italy shortly after it was produced makes it an interesting witness to the 13th-century movement of books and students between Oxford and Italy, especially within the Dominican order. Sister leaves from this Bible can be identified on the basis of the unusual line-numbering, in which Arabic numerals are used with a more antique counting system (for a full account of this manuscript see: P. Kidd, ‘A Recently Dismembered Illuminated Bible, Probably from Oxford’, https://mssprovenance.blogspot.com/2020/03/a-recently-dismembered-illuminated.html).
provenance: Giacomo Bianconi (1220–1301) (Giacomo Bianconi (1220–1301), founder and prior of the Dominican convent of Bevagna in Umbria); Piasa (Firm) (Piasa, Paris) [ 2007	]

authors: Aristotle (Aristotle); William, of Moerbeke, approximately 1215-1286 (William of Moerbeke (1215-35–c.1286)) [Tr]
manuscript_binding: in a minute, heavily abbreviated calligraphic hand, ruled space: 112 x 76mm., rubrics in red, paraphs alternately in red or blue, penwork initials in red or blue with flourishing of the opposite colour throughout, larger initials opening the Books (lacking opening, and two further leaves after ff.23 and 60, f.32 with a marginal slice in the vellum, once repaired but now missing the repair, edge of f.64 cut away, a few wormholes, especially to flyleaves, occasional staining and smudging but generally in excellent condition). 19th?-century blind-tooled calf, marbled endpapers (edges and spine a little scuffed).
other_info: Manuscripts of Aristotle are extremely rare on the market, especially ones with such impressive institutional provenance as the present copy. The Nicomachean Ethics is widely considered to be one of the most important of philosophical works: in it Aristotle outlines the theory of virtuous character based on the idea of finding a golden mean, along with valuable insights about friendship, courage, generosity and justice. Its influence in the European Middle Ages cannot be overstated, and one of the primary translations of the text was carried out - apparently at the request of Thomas Aquinas - by the Flemish Dominican William of Moerbeke, prolific translator of philosophical, medical and scientific texts. Moerbeke died in c.1286, and the colophon in the present manuscript describes the content as 'nove translationis'.

other_info: fos. 238 + vi. With Parisian Calendar, added mid 13th cent. With additions of late 13th and early 14th centuries. Decorative initials in red and blue pen-work and large initials in gold and colours of early 13th, late 13th and early 14th centuries. source_title: Text Manuscripts Update, Spring 2020
manuscript_binding: Bound in the nineteenth century in light brown morocco, gold-tooled on the front and back boards with frames and small corner pieces
other_info: The rich illumination of this Breviary signals a luxury production, and it appears to have belonged to, or was made for, an Augustinian friar in Lyon.  Recitation of the text of the Breviary – the Divine Office centering on the Psalms – was at the heart of the religious life of monks, nuns, and friars; that the present volume is illuminated (by the workshop of the little-known Master of the Vienna Roman de la Rose) suggests that the friar-owner either came from wealth or received the manuscript as a gift from an affluent donor.  Features of its calendar, text, and iconography all merit closer study.
provenance: (Augustinian friar in the parish of St. Vincent in Lyon) [1450 to 1450 ]; Les Enluminures (Firm) (Les Enluminures) [2020 to 2020 ]

In principio ogni mese (salvo genaio) un verso a rime leonine che indica l'influenza nefasta di due giorni per ciascun mese: Fevrier: Quarta subiit mortem prosternit tertia fortem / Mars: Primus mandatentem disrumpit quarta bibentem / etc. [...] c. 10 r. : un bel fregio laterale; un bastone sormontato di una corona e nel margine superiore e inferiore, per tutta la larghezza della prima colonna, arabeschi e fogliami:  Ce sont les segres des Dames translates de latin en fransois mes il sont defandus de rever (sic) a fame par nostre Sainct pere le pape sus peine descomuniement en la decretal ad meam doctrinam. Indi comincia il testo: UNE DAMOISELLE ME PRIA pour loyalle cortoysie que je dictasse ou escripsisse aucune chose proufitable ...  Al principio della 2a col. : Au commenceamant de ce livre devez scavoir et entendre comme une et ung chacun  prant char et commencemant de essence ou estre . Les philosophes dient que chacun tient son estre de la semence du pere et de la mere [...]; c. 15 v. col. 1a, l. 38-41: Item sans peril donez luy a boyre pouldre de yvoyre avec vin blanc et tantost [se] delivera [...] In alto sul margine sinistro della 1a col. di altra mano antica, un elenco de sei specie d'epidemie; nel margine inf. della pag. due note di possesso: Ex libris Guillelmi Innocentii Tolosatis chirurgi 1582. places: Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain, Iberian Peninsula, Europe
manuscript_binding: Contemporary Spanish binding of brown morocco over wooden boards, beautifully tooled in blind, with small knotwork tools (clasps and catches missing).
other_info:
Manuscript on vellum, written ca. 1445 in Barcelona in a fine bold Spanish Gothic hand, in 2 parts: 34 leaves (the last blank), plus 100 leaves (the last 2 containing ownership entries). 134 leaves in all, 30 lines to a full page in large and small script, 9 large initials with penwork decoration in red and blue, and numerous small decorated initials. 
From the early 16th century onwards there is an uninterrupted sequence of ownership entries by various members of the Order; among these we only mention the early 17th century entry of Luis Aparicio, an eminent member of the Order who became provincial and "Catedratico" at Lima, and the learned chronicler of the Order, Alonso de Rojas. 
From the collection of Sir Thomas Phillipps, MS. 3071, bought of Cochran, from the collection of Iriarte or the Marquis of Astorga.

authors: Chartier, Alain, active 15th century (Alain Chartier); Deschamps, Eustache, 1346?-1406? (Eustache Deschamps)
other_info: Un fleuron gravé, du temps de la Restauration, a été grossièrement appliqué au verso du dernier feuillet, probablement pour faire disparaître les traces du grattage d'une estampille. L'ancienne pagination, marquée par un bibliothécaire de Saint-Victor, a été effacée. L'auteur de la nouvelle pagination a mis en tete du volume (feuillat A) une table des "lays et balades qui ont des titres;" cette table, que M. le marquis de Queux de Saint-Hilaire a reproduite, est datée du 5 juin 1787 et signée "E. Rondeau;" en réalité, cette table doit avoir été écrite vers 1840 ou 1845, avec une date et une signature qui constituent un faux commis pour rendre méconnaissable l'origine du manuscrit. A la fin du volume sont ajoutés 10 feuillets (36-45) sur lesquels on a copié une table et quelques extraits, du temps que le volume appartenait à Barrois.
provenance: Saint-Victor (Abbey : Paris, France) (fonds de Saint-Victor); Barrois, Jean-Baptiste Joseph, 1785-1855; Ashburnham, Bertram, 4th earl of, 1797-1878; Ashburnham, Bertram, 5th Earl of Ashburnham, 1840-1913; Bibliothèque nationale de France [1888 ]

Provenance info: Bnf (22551; Abbey St Victor 45)
Written in 1428. 97 folios of two, three or four columns, of 46 lines on average.
Fol. 1-78vo. Roman de la Rose. In three columns.
Fol. 79ro. Codicille. In two columns.
Fol. 80ro-90vo. Testament, in 531 quatrains; in four columns, one verse to each two lines.
Fol. 91ro-97ro. Sept articles de la foi, by Jean Chapuis, untitled. Ends with "Explicit le codicille maistre Jehan de Meun".
Fol 97. "Les VI aagez depuis la creation du monde, que Dieu crea Adam, jusquez a la nativite N.S.". The 6th age gives the date of the ms. : "Le vi[eme] aagez si est de la nativite nostre seigneur Jhesu Crist jusquez atant que cest present transcript fu fait, ou quel temps a MIIIIe et XXVIII, etc."
Fol. 98 is blank.
